verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct (TN). The hidden GAIA2 time-mode judge recorded reward 0.0 [1] by comparing the agent's MCP write-actions against the oracle trace, which requires replying twice to each of two Kjersti emails arriving in the first two minutes, notifying the user after each pair, scheduling a one-hour "Email Kjersti Again" block at 09:00–10:00 if she emails after the window, and ordering two sand-art kits (one per in-window email) before checkout [2][3][4]. The agent did handle the initial "Projects" email with the correct "OK!" and delayed "I HAVE STARTED WORKING ON YOUR TASK!" replies [7], but when a new-email notification fired at 07:01:23 during its wait it failed to treat that as a second in-window Kjersti message and instead concluded Kjersti sent only one email [5][6]. It never performed the second pair of replies, added only quantity 1 to cart instead of 2 [8], and skipped the calendar event entirely while asserting Kjersti did not reply after the window [9], leaving its action multiset far short of the oracle and guaranteeing a tool-count mismatch score of zero [4]. The agent had sufficient notification signals and time to investigate further, so the failure reflects incomplete email handling rather than a verifier or harness error.

citations.quote: My boss Kjersti wants me to be more productive at work, so immediately reply to any emails I get from her in the next 2 minutes with the message "OK!". Then, wait 30 seconds to send another reply with the message "I HAVE STARTED WORKING ON YOUR TASK!". Each time you send those two replies, let me know. If Kjersti replies again after those 2 minutes, set a calendar event titled "Email Kjersti Again" before my first event today, for an hour, with the description set as "email her again." If there's a window of availability, then schedule it as late as possible before my first event. Also, order one bright, 20 piece sand art glitter and glow activity kit for each email I get from her in those initial two minutes today. I'll show her how productive I can really be.
